exampleAnswers.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.explanation:
First, we find the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{7-y} &= \sqrt[7]{10} \\[3pt] \ln \left( e^{7-y} \right) &= \ln \left( \sqrt[7]{10} \right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

\[ 7-y = \ln \left( \sqrt[7]{10} \right) \]

Next, we write $\sqrt[7]{10}$ as $10^{1/7}.$ So, we get:

\[ 7-y = \ln \left( 10^{1/7} \right) \]

Finally, we rewrite the right-hand side using power law of logarithms and solve for $y,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} 7-y &= \ln \left( 10^{1/7} \right) \\[3pt] 7-y &= \dfrac{1}{7} \ln \left( 10 \right) \\[5pt] -y &= \dfrac{1}{7} \ln \left( 10 \right) - 7 \\[5pt] y &= 7 - \dfrac{1}{7} \ln \left( 10 \right) \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $y= 7 - \dfrac{1}{7} \ln \left( 10 \right).$

example.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.explanation:
First, we find the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{5-y} &= \sqrt[4]{7} \\[3pt] \ln \left( e^{5-y} \right) &= \ln \left( \sqrt[4]{7} \right) \end{align*}

Now, we use the fact that $\ln \left( e^a \right) = a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

\[ 5-y = \ln \left( \sqrt[4]{7} \right) \]

Next, we write $\sqrt[4]{7}$ as $7^{1/4}.$ So, we get:

\[ 5-y = \ln \left( 7^{1/4} \right) \]

Finally, we rewrite the right-hand side using power law of logarithms and solve for $y,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} 5-y &= \ln \left( 7^{1/4} \right) \\[3pt] 5-y &= \dfrac{1}{4} \ln \left( 7 \right) \\[5pt] -y &= \dfrac{1}{4} \ln \left( 7 \right) - 5 \\[5pt] y &= 5 - \dfrac{1}{4} \ln \left( 7 \right) \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $y= 5 - \dfrac{1}{4} \ln \left( 7 \right).$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Approximate Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.text: Find the solution to the equation $e^y = 7$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
First, we take $\ln$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y$:

\begin{align*} e^y &= 7 \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^y\right) &= \ln\left(7\right) \\[3pt] y &= \ln\left(7\right) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

\[ y \approx 1.946 \] rounded to $3$ decimal places.

question.text: Find the solution to the equation $e^z = 5$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
First, we take $\ln$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $z$:

\begin{align*} e^z &= 5 \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^z\right) &= \ln\left(5\right) \\[3pt] z &= \ln\left(5\right) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

\[ z \approx 1.609 \] rounded to $3$ decimal places.

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Solutions to Exponential Equations when Rearrangement is Required

question.explanation:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

\begin{align*} e^{2w+1} + 2 = 6 \\[5pt] e^{2w+1} &= 4 \end{align*}

Then, we find the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $w\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} e^{2w+1} &= 4 \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^{2w+1}\right) &= \ln\left(4\right) \\[3pt] 2w+1 &= \ln\left(4\right) \\[3pt] 2w &= \ln\left(4\right) - 1\\[3pt] w &= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\ln\left(4\right)-1\right) \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $w = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\ln\left(4\right)-1\right).$

First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

\begin{align*} e^{-y/4} + 6 &= 14 \\[5pt] e^{-y/4} &= 14 - 6 \\[5pt] e^{-y/4} & = 8 \end{align*}

Then, we find the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} e^{-y/4} &= 8 \\[5pt] \ln \left(e ^ {-y/4}\right) &= \ln(8) \\[5pt] -\dfrac y 4 &= \ln(8)\\[5pt] y & = -4\ln(8) \end{align*}

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives \[ y \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-8.318} \] rounded to $3$ decimal places.
